abstract: Lipid droplets (LDs) are dynamic organelles that communicate with other cellular components to orchestrate energetic homeostasis and signaling transduction. In skeletal muscle, the presence and importance of LDs has been widely studied in myofibers of both rodents and humans under physiological conditions and in metabolic disorders. Yet, the role of LDs in the myogenic stem cells has only begun to be unveiled. In this review, we briefly summarize the process of LD biogenesis and degradation in the most prevalent model; we then review the recent knowledge on LDs in skeletal muscle and muscle stem cells. We further introduce some advanced methodologies in LD imaging and mass spectrometry that have propelled the understanding of the dynamics and heterogeneity of LDs.
